newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee surges by 8 pct, ends near peak.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee surges by 8 pct, ends near peak.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures surged by eight percent in late Tuesday afternoon on panic commission house buying, a rebound in New York and on bullish U.S. consumer stock data, traders said.

Although prices edged back slightly, they still ended the day near the session's ceiling. Benchmark September recaptured its foothold above the $1,900 mark for the first time in a week, ending the day at $1,910 for a steep $132 gain.
The contract was earlier driven to the day's high of $1,920, a 8.0 percent rise on the day. Front-month July also soared by $139 at $1,890.
Traders noted panic buying of the July and September contracts by one major brokerage, possibly acting on behalf of a leading European trade house.
The July discount to September narrowed further to $20 by the close on Tuesday from $28 on Monday.
Traders said worries about low certifiable coffee for July delivery could allow the front-month contract to command a premium over September in the next few sessions.
July's first notice day is July 1. LIFFE reported on Monday that certified stocks fell to 881 five-tonne lots in May from 4,858 in April.
"Why the delayed reaction I don't know," said one trader. "This shows that there is no coffee and tendering is going to be against harder specifications."
LIFFE's new grading rules take effect with the July contract onwards.
New York's rise followed overnight news of a 122,000 bag rise in U.S. consumer coffee stocks which was at the lower end of trade expectations.
Broker GNI Ltd said that at 1.97 million bags they were still well down on last year's 2.27 million but noted that the stocks had already started to trend lower by this stage last year.
Volume totalled 12,146 lots. -- Jalil Hamid, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4985
